research_concepts: regular season to playoff context shift
methodological_questions: Can cut-heavy and drive-heavy shaper classes be defined reliably from play-type labels?
Is n=24 units enough to compare role transfer between the two classes?
Do play-type labels in the derived records have adequate accuracy for this comparison?
How is 'travels better' operationalised across seasons, playoffs, or matchups?

historical_evidence.finding: Team-level RS vs playoff PPP by play type (25 teams, min 30 possessions per cell, no CIs): DRIVE PPP was 1.198 in the regular season and 0.912 in the playoffs (-0.286). PNR was -0.173, PULL_UP +0.301, others within -0.07. Recorded as motivating a playoff DRIVE exclusion.

Play-type labelling audit found OTHER PPP inflated by foul-ending possessions (36% of OTHER end in fouls), DRIVE 12pp below the foul benchmark, and initiation_type mapping only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) to a real play type. Verdict recorded as artifact_found.

Play-type label accuracy audit failed overall: OTHER 20.2% against a <10% target, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark, most PT PPP above benchmark, and identity checks failed. Verdict recorded as tool_eval_fail.

Cross-possession decay gate failed: DRIVE lifts were flat across lags (+0.015 to +0.021), within-team lag-1 effect ranged from +0.015 to -0.002, effect sizes were about d 0.01-0.03 with p near 0 from n>150k, and a team-quality confound was recorded. Verdict failed_gate.

Similarity of replacement play-type profiles did not separate absorption from cascade (ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman -0.19, wrong-signed). Observational sample and power were not recorded.
DRIVE PPP rose across playoff series buckets (0.889 to 0.949, +0.060), with no clear signal. Pooled 1197 records, no CIs, observational with selection caveats; mechanism recorded as unclear.

Pattern-module stability was unstable (stability CV 0.919) across 23 games and 46 team-observations, with tautological keys and about 6.9 observations per key. Recommended merging into possession_flow.

Across 52 series (104 playoff team-offense units), no conditional pivot branch met the durability bar (durable_branches empty). Median net swing was CUT +0.36, DRIVE -0.27, POST_UP -0.22. The record's unit listing was truncated in the retrieved text.
TOV_FORCE matchup decomposition on four playoff games: team-PT lifts were small, while player-channel lifts were large on small n (cell n about 15-54). No holdout or game-outcome check.

Playoff adaptation-pair sustainability across 74 matchups (pair n 5 to 44): 10 of 12 pairs were within 0.10 of non-pivot, and two pairs with enough signal were PIVOT_LOSES. Recorded as B_powered_null with small-sample limitation.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Deriving play-type class from initiation_type mapping and comparing play-type PPP
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: foul-ending possessions leaked into OTHER and DRIVE; initiation_type mapped only 0.7% of possessions to a real play type.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type label accuracy and distribution audit
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as tool_eval_fail: OTHER share was 20.2% against a target under 10%, 40.8% of labels were low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw was off benchmark, and identity checks failed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Cross-possession decay (lag) test of play-type memory
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as failed_gate: lifts were flat rather than decaying, collapsed under a within-team baseline, and carried a team-quality confound (LIM:confounding).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type profile similarity to separate absorption from cascade
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive with a wrong-signed correlation and a label-error limitation; sample and power were not recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Tracking play-type PPP across playoff series game buckets
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear: no clear signal, observational data with selection and regression-to-the-mean caveats, and no CIs.
Recorded as A_unanswerable: stability CV 0.919, tautological keys, and about 6.9 observations per key across 23 games.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-channel matchup decomposition on four playoff games
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with EXPOSURE_SPARSITY: player-channel cells of about 15-28 defensive possessions and helper-steal attribution noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Sustained PPP after pivoting to a listed counter in playoff matchups
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as B_powered_null with small sample (pair n 5 to 44); two pairs showed PIVOT_LOSES, and population deltas were mostly under 0.10.

evidence_establishes: Play-type labels derived from this pipeline have documented accuracy problems: foul leakage into OTHER and DRIVE, low initiation_type coverage, and failed identity checks (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014).
DRIVE-associated PPP fell sharply from regular season to playoffs in one team-level comparison (FAM:SF-APPS-011, supported, no CIs).

Earlier attempts to test play-type memory, pivots, and replacement similarity in this project did not yield a robust, powered positive result (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPM-054, FAM:SF-CHT-052, FAM:SF-APPS-049).
No retrieved record tests whether cut-heavy shaper roles transfer better than drive-heavy roles.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether cut-heavy shaper roles transfer better than drive-heavy roles. No retrieved record defines or tests shaper classes or a transfer metric.

Whether DRIVE's regular-season-to-playoff PPP drop reflects role transfer, labelling error, or team-quality composition, since the supporting record has no CIs and its labels are contested by the audits.
Any estimate at n=24 units. No retrieved record reports a power analysis for a 24-unit comparison.
Whether the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data version in the current pipeline has the same labelling defects as the retrieved studies, which may have used other data versions.
own_inferences: The question's key term 'travel' is undefined. Without an operational transfer metric, no test can be pre-registered.
With 24 units, detecting a moderate class difference in transfer would need a very large effect or many repeated units per shaper, which the data does not provide.

Cut-heavy versus drive-heavy classes are likely confounded with team quality, role, usage, and position, and the retrieved records show team-quality confounding is already a documented failure mode (FAM:SF-CHT-029).

The strongest retrieved signal (FAM:SF-APPS-011) is about DRIVE PPP falling into the playoffs, which is related to the question but not the same estimand. It is also weakened by the labelling failures in FAM:SF-CHT-025 and FAM:SF-APPM-014.
uncertainties: The retrieved records do not state whether the current data version (2022-23 to 2025-26, with partial 2025-26 playoffs before 2026-06-21) is the same one used in earlier studies.
The text of FAM:SF-APPS-049 and FAM:SF-APPA-066 was truncated in the retrieved results, so their full unit lists and any further results are unknown. Read_family was not called.
No CIs were recorded in several supporting records, so effect magnitudes are uncertain.
Whether 'cut-heavy' and 'drive-heavy' shapers can be classified reliably from the derived records is untested.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show repeated labelling failures (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014), a team-quality confound (FAM:SF-CHT-029), and several underpowered or unstable tests (FAM:SF-CHT-028, FAM:SF-APPA-066, FAM:SF-APPM-054). Together they move the decision from a standard test to do_not_proceed as posed. A minimum viable test is specified below, contingent on label validation.

research_concepts: playoff versus regular season role stability
methodological_questions: can role transferability be tested with n=24 units
how should cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shaper classes be defined from play-type possession records
what sample size and exposure is needed to compare role transfer between shaper types
how to handle role stability measurement reliability across seasons and playoff contexts
args.query: cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shapers structural roles transfer across seasons and playoffs with play-by-play derived play-type possession records, small sample n=24

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)

- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
